svg.text: Buildings, districts and landmarks: the silhouette chart

Twenty faceted shapes, eight district looks and five landmarks, all original and generic. Every building is a prism with at most three roof facets. Working labels, pending Legal review. Brief: docs/art/district-looks.md.
A. The twenty shapes (new shapes are marked; each is drawn at its own scale, with one fighter for scale)
a plain tall prism, a low plant box on top
two or three setbacks, the top tier 60 percent wide
the top corners chamfered in one facet: a cut gem
a shaft under a four-sided pyramid; rare, never a
a near-square mid-rise, parapet and plant box
a long low box, shallow gable, door panels
a long low building under a run of saw teeth
a tall octagonal stack, tapered, flared cap
a box under a 35 to 40 degree gable
a house under a steep (55 degree), deep-eaved roof
a house in three stone steps up a slope
a house with a wide front and a flat awning facet
a lean-to with one roof facet
a long gable with a stepped porch
a gable with a three-sided belfry at one end
a long low platform with post stubs
a mast with a long faceted jib, off centre
a thin pole with a yard arm
an octagonal tapering tower, lantern room, cone
B. The eight looks, as a street of the district's own shapes at the district's data heights (the window pattern and the palette lane are the look)
62 bh median, up to 260 (one fighter for scale; widths drawn 3 times wider)
Uneven and tall, rising to the middle: continuous glass bands between pale piers, flat roofs with plant boxes, setbacks and chamfers.
25 bh median, up to 45 (one fighter for scale)
A wall of slabs with regular gaps: two horizontal window strips a storey, pale sills, a parapet.
4.5 bh median, up to 6 (one fighter for scale)
Low, small and rhythmic: repeated gables with small windows, two or three to a facade, one direction per block.
6 bh median, up to 10 (one fighter for scale)
Long and low, broken by tall stacks: a clerestory strip under the roof, big door panels, sawtooth or shallow gable.
5 bh median, up to 10 (one fighter for scale)
Low sheds along a quay, with crane and mast verticals and one lighthouse: few windows, wide doors, a loft hatch.
4.5 bh median, up to 7 (one fighter for scale)
Cool white cottages stepping down to the quay: small square windows with blue shutters, a horizontal rhythm.
4.5 bh median, up to 6 (one fighter for scale)
Brick and soot: sawtooth sheds and kiln stacks, small square windows in dark frames, repeated verticals with smoke.
4.5 bh median, up to 7 (one fighter for scale)
Stone and straw on a slope: tiny windows in thick walls, steep thatch, stepped diagonals.
C. The five landmarks (one fighter for scale; heights from settlements.json)
The Gatebell: a stone shaft with an open four-arch
belfry, a dark bell cone, an eight-sided spire and an
Legal (RL-040): no clock face, and never a spire over
A banded octagonal stack in pale stone and soot grey
bands, a wide flared cap and a short side flue.
An octagonal tapering tower in two plain wide bands
(pale stone, slate), a faceted lantern room of pale cyan
Legal (RL-040): plain wide bands only; no spiral,
diagonal or black-and-white banding; no beam.
A long timber hall with a steep central gable, a stepped
porch and a small faceted lantern on the ridge.
A stone chapel on a terrace step with a steep thatch
roof and a small three-sided belfry at one end; the bell
Faceted rule kept: prisms, octagonal stacks and three roof facets at most. Nothing here reproduces a real landmark, and no fighter lane hue (teal, orchid, moss, coral) or mid blue is a building mass.
